packages/show-planner/src/corrections.ts.content: Both branches of the pinned-cue reconciliation increment `applied`, so a pinned cue whose ID is no longer present in the plan is still counted as applied and is never added to `noLongerApply`. This silently hides lost pin edits after a planner upgrade (the exact thing this function is meant to surface) and inflates `applied`. The two branches are effectively dead code because they do the same thing.

The pinned filter only excludes IDs already in `keptIds`, never IDs produced by the newly generated `fresh` cues. Because cue IDs are deterministic (`seed:section:level:ordinal`), a pinned cue can carry the same ID as a fresh cue that survives the filter above, so the returned `cues` array contains two cues with an identical ID. Downstream consumers keying by ID would then lose or corrupt one of them. Exclude fresh IDs (or fold the pinned cues into the same dedupe set) before appending.

This coverage predicate is inconsistent with `inLockedRegion`, which is the predicate actually used by `regenerateWithLocks`. Coverage here only checks the cue's `startBeat` against the half-open range `[startBeat, endBeat)`, whereas `inLockedRegion` requires the cue's full span (`startBeat + durationBeats <= r.endBeat`). As a result a lock can be reported as `applied` by `applyEdits` even though regeneration would not preserve any cue in it. Additionally, `cues` still contains cues listed in `edits.deletedCueIds`, so a region that only covers deleted cues is also (mis)reported as applying. Align the containment test with `inLockedRegion` and ignore deleted cue IDs.

analysis/src/autolight_analysis/config_s.content: Root schema only declares `type: object` + a `properties` map and never sets `additionalProperties: false`, while every real contract (enums and numeric ranges) exists only in prose `description`. Consequences: (a) misspelled/unknown config keys are silently accepted instead of being rejected (the very spelling risk this file's review targets); (b) clearly invalid values such as `runtime.clock.tickHz: 10000` or `runtime.host: "banana"` pass validation. Add `additionalProperties: false` (or `patternProperties`) and promote the documented enums/ranges to `enum`/`minimum`/`maximum`.

The default `"\"\" (none)"` is a human-readable sentinel (it literally contains quote characters and a parenthetical), not a usable device id. Any layer that applies schema defaults verbatim will set the capture device id to the literal string `"" (none)`. Use the empty string or `null` as the default.

Intended value is a boolean (description says `bool [spec 110]`, and the sibling `analysis.ml.enabled` is `boolean`), but `type` is `string` and the default is prose `"true during Live"`. Validation accepts any string and consumers expecting a boolean receive a string. Declare `type: boolean` with default `true`.

Keepalive is a millisecond duration (0 = disabled) but the property is typed `string` with default `"0 (off)"`. A consumer expecting a number of milliseconds gets a non-numeric string. Use `type: number` with default `0`.
`colorQuantizeLevels` is a per-channel count (0 = off) but is typed `string` with default `"0 (off)"`. Use `type: number` with default `0` so numeric consumers are not handed a string.

`flx4.hints.enabled` is described as a `list` of hint types but is typed `string` with the prose default `"all hint types"`. Any consumer that iterates the enabled hints as a list will receive a string and silently iterate characters / fail. Type it as `array` (with `items`) or `boolean`, with a concrete default.

`neverDuringLive` describes a boolean invariant (`read-only invariant`) but is typed `string`. A consumer checking a boolean guard will never match this string and the invariant will not be enforced. Declare `type: boolean` with default `true`.

The default `"[] (all eligible)"` is a string sentinel, not the empty-array value the description implies. A consumer reading `interfaces` as an array will get a string. Use `default: []` with `type: array` and `items: { type: string }`.

Same defect as `govee.lan.interfaces`: default `"[] (all eligible)"` is a string, not an array; consumers expecting a list of interface names will receive a string. Use `default: []` with `type: array` / `items: { type: string }`.

The default is a stringified map (`"{ weight: 1, ... }"`), not a JSON object; consumers expecting a map will receive an unparseable string. The same stringified-map-as-default anti-pattern appears for `planner.sectionEnergy`, `planner.evaluation.bounds`, `analysis.bands`, `planner.events.minConfidence`, `qa.events.minRecall` and `qa.events.minPrecision`. Replace these with real object/array defaults (and pin the type accordingly).

`<fixtureId>` is literal text inside the JSON object key, so no real per-device key (e.g. `govee.device.H61A0.transportMode`) will ever match this property; per-device overrides are therefore never validated (same for `govee.device.<fixtureId>.transportOrder`). Model this with `patternProperties` (e.g. `^govee\.device\..+\.transportMode$`) or a nested `govee.device` object schema.

`*` is literal in the key, so per-shortcut entries like `ui.shortcuts.blackout` can never match this property and go unvalidated. The same applies to `qa.faults.*`. Use `patternProperties` (e.g. `^ui\.shortcuts\.`) so the real dynamic keys are covered.
